extraction.name: Prompted Textures Dataset (PTD)
extraction.description: A texture dataset spanning 246,285 images across 56 texture classes, generated using text-to-image models with texture-specific prompts and a three-stage refinement process consisting of frequency analysis, patch variance filtering, and CLIP scoring.
extraction.creator: Blaine Hoak, Patrick McDaniel
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Images were generated using Stable Diffusion text-to-image models with texture-specific prompts. Prompts were constructed by combining descriptors from categories including artistic style, spatial arrangement, color enhancers, colors, and texture types, resulting in 96,768 unique prompts. Five images were generated per prompt.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Images generated from Stable Diffusion model using constructed texture prompts. The prompts were based on 56 texture classes (47 from Describable Textures Dataset plus 9 additional classes) combined with artistic, spatial, color enhancer, and color descriptors.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Images flagged as NSFW by the Stable Diffusion safety filter were regenerated to ensure a consistent number of images per prompt. Flagged images were excluded from the final dataset.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: A three-stage refinement process was applied: (1) Frequency filtering using Fourier transforms to remove object-like images by retaining the top 80% of images with highest frequency cutoff values; (2) Patch variance filtering to eliminate homogeneous images by removing the bottom 20% with lowest mean patch variance; (3) CLIP score filtering to ensure prompt alignment by removing the bottom 20% with lowest CLIP scores. This reduced the dataset from 483,840 to 246,285 images.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Human evaluation was conducted with 9 participants who evaluated 100 images each (900 unique images total). Participants rated each image on two questions: (1) overall quality and (2) how well the image represents the provided descriptor, using a scale of 1 to 5.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Human evaluation scores were analyzed across different refinement stages to validate the effectiveness of each filtering step. Mean quality and representativeness scores were computed, showing gradual improvement through refinement with an overall 3.4% increase in quality and 4.5% increase in representativeness. CLIP scores were found to align well with human representative scores.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: Each of the 900 evaluated images received one quality rating and one representativeness rating from a single participant.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: 9 participants were recruited to evaluate the images
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Stable Diffusion model from HuggingFace was used for image generation. CLIP (Contrastive Language-Image Pre-training) was used for computing alignment scores between images and text prompts. Fourier transforms were used for frequency analysis. Inception model was used for computing Inception Scores.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset enables research on texture bias in machine learning models, which has implications for understanding model trustworthiness and interpretability. The dataset has been used to develop Texture Object Association Values (TAV) metric for measuring texture bias, revealing that texture type can affect model accuracy by up to 66% and that 90% of natural adversarial examples contained misaligned texture information.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset generation process encountered challenges with NSFW filtering, where up to 60% of initially generated images were flagged despite using benign prompts. Certain texture descriptors like 'paisley' consistently triggered the filter. Some texture classes performed better than others in quality metrics, with textures appearing in common objects (e.g., hairy, flaky) achieving better scores, while more structured textures (e.g., grid, polka-dotted) had worse scores. Certain word pair combinations in prompts yielded lower quality images, particularly 'muted' and 'earthy' descriptors with subtle textures.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset is generated synthetically using Stable Diffusion and may not fully capture all characteristics of real-world textures. There is variation in quality across texture classes, with structured textures showing room for improvement. The NSFW safety filter posed challenges and may have introduced unintended biases in the generation process. Some descriptor combinations (e.g., 'muted', 'earthy') tend to produce lower quality images. The dataset is limited to 56 texture classes.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is designed for texture-based research including: understanding high-level features models learn, uncovering biases, identifying security vulnerabilities, measuring texture bias in models, constructing texture-object associations, and studying adversarial examples. It has been used to develop the Texture Object Association Values (TAV) metric for measuring texture bias. The dataset can be adapted for other tasks by replacing texture descriptors with other types (e.g., shape descriptors).

name.evidence: In this work, we introduce an extensible methodology for generating high-quality, diverse texture images, which we use to create the Prompted Textures Dataset (PTD), a new texture dataset spanning 246,285 images across 56 texture classes.

rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis.evidence: At each step in the refinement process, we can see that both quality and representativeness of the data improves from the previous step, confirming that each part of our refinement process leads to improved dataset quality. Combining all refinement steps together provides us with an overall 3.4% increase in quality and a 4.5% increase in representativeness.
